messages:
maya: Heads-up — multiple support tickets reporting p99 spikes on hosted text-generation endpoints since ~11:10. Customers seeing p99 3–8s (baseline ~1.1s). I’m seeing GPU memory pressure and a few OOMs on gpu-rw-62, allocator errors in the runtime logs. Attaching quick logs below.

support-bot: Created INC-2026-1423 and linked to customer tickets <https://support.example/INC-2026-1423> :white_check_mark:

liam: any recent model or config rollouts to that pool?

maya: We rolled out model redwood-alpha-v2.3-quant at 11:05 to the hosted pool that backs gpu-rw-62. Canary looked fine but traffic ramped faster than predicted.

jordan: Can you paste the p95/p99 times and a snippet of the allocator logs?

maya: Metrics snippet:
```
window 10m: p50 220ms, p95 980ms, p99 3600ms
node gpu-rw-62: GPU mem used 98%, free 200MB, OOM_count +4 in 15m
runtime allocator: slab_alloc failed, attempting compaction, freed 0 bytes
KV cache size: 145GB -> growth +20GB in 12m
```

eva: That pattern (KV growth + slab_alloc failing to compact) smells like fragmentation after quantized kernels touch lots of small KV allocations. Quick mitigations: enable slab compaction and stricter KV eviction on the pool, and roll a graceful restart of runtime daemons on the node.

liam: Can you list the exact commands to apply? I’ll run them on the affected cluster.

maya: Quick steps I recommend (do one at a time):
1) Patch pool config to lower KV target and force eviction:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap pool-gpu-rw-62 --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/kv_eviction_threshold","value":"0.75"}]'
```
2) Enable slab compaction env var on runtime daemonset (immediate effect after restart):
```bash
kubectl -n runtime set env daemonset/gpu-runtime ALLOC_SLAB_COMPACT=1
kubectl -n runtime rollout restart daemonset/gpu-runtime
```
3) If pressure persists, scale the pool up by +2 nodes OR fallback routing to v2.2 (smaller KV usage):
```bash
# scale nodes via autoscaler profile
curl -X POST "https://infra-api.internal/pools/gpu-rw-62/scale" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"delta":2}'
# or pin traffic to v2.2
redwoodctl routes set --pool gpu-rw-62 --model redwood-alpha-v2.2
```

jordan: Thanks — I’ll run 1+2 now on the staging subset, then apply to prod if metrics improve. For repro locally, I can run the synthetic KV churn script:
```bash
# repro: hot loop that grows per-request KV entries
python tools/repro/kvgrowth.py --model v2.3 --seq-len 1024 --qps 40 --runtime gpu --duration 10m
```

maya: Running the patches on prod pool now. ETA ~4m for rollout.

liam: Also grabbing a heap/fragmentation dump from the allocator (will upload). If allocator shows many small free slabs, we need a long-term tune: increase slab bucket sizes and tune free-list coalescing.

alex: Update — after enabling ALLOC_SLAB_COMPACT and lowering KV eviction threshold, p99 dropped from ~3600ms -> ~1.4s within two rollout waves. GPU memory usage reduced to ~86%. No new OOMs observed in the last 8m.

maya: Great, marking this as mitigated. Action items:
- engineering/runtime: follow-up allocator tuning (increase slab coalescing, revisit bucket sizing)
- ml/ops: evaluate v2.3 KV footprint and look for model changes that cause disproportionate KV growth
- support: notify affected customers with post-mortem and mitigation steps

jordan: I’ll open a tracking RFC for allocator changes and include repro + metric dashboards.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-1423 transitioned to RESOLVED by maya at 3176550020.

support-bot: Customer notes appended to tickets and customers notified.

alex: please keep this thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
